description: The Weeping Mirror manifests as a faintly luminous sphere of distorted space, its surface rippling like water disturbed by invisible stones. Through its translucent boundary, observers can glimpse fragmentary images of ships and stations that have passed through across centuries—some vessels long destroyed, others not yet built. Sensors detect a complex chrono-particle signature that pulses with mathematical regularity, each emission carrying data from multiple timeframes simultaneously.

The anomaly breathes in a 7.3-hour cycle, drawing temporal echoes inward during contraction and releasing them during expansion. Ships passing through during the contraction phase often encounter their own reflections from previous or future transits, leading to the unnerving experience of watching oneself depart while still arriving. The intensity peaks every 72 hours, during which the boundary between echoes and reality grows dangerously thin.

Discovered in 2612 by the cartography vessel Silent Meridian, the anomaly earned its name from the first captain's log entry describing 'a mirror that weeps the tears of time.' The Temporal Sciences Consortium has maintained a permanent research station at safe distance since 2715, though three expeditions into the core have resulted in crews returning with fragmented memories spanning decades they never lived.

The Weeping Mirror remains one of the most studied and least understood temporal phenomena in charted space. Rumors persist of a coherent intelligence within the echoes—patterns too consistent to be random, responses too appropriate to be coincidence. Salvage crews occasionally attempt to recover ships trapped in echo states, though the Consortium officially discourages such operations. For those willing to risk temporal displacement, the anomaly offers something rare: a chance to send messages backward, or to hear whispers from futures yet unwritten.
